user.text:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

history.assistant:
The reading list is a small local app with no accounts. Start it with `npm start` and open http://127.0.0.1:3000.

The home page splits books into Currently reading and Finished. Add a book from the form, open it for the title, author, and notes, and use Mark finished when you are done. Each book has its own address, shown on the book page, such as http://127.0.0.1:3000/books/<id>. Anyone with that link can see the title, author, and notes.

Books are saved in `data/books.json` and stay there after a restart. The server only listens on this machine. `npm test` passed, 7 tests, exit code 0.

{"action":"run","command":"set -e
base=http://127.0.0.1:3456
curl -sf "$base/" | head -n 20
echo '---'
curl -sf -D - -o /tmp/add-book.html -X POST "$base/books" \
  --data-urlencode 'title=The Left Hand of Darkness' \
  --data-urlencode 'author=Ursula K. Le Guin' \
  --data-urlencode 'notes=Winter on Gethen.' \
  | head -n 20
echo '--- file ---'
cat /tmp/reading-smoke.json
echo '--- detail ---'
loc=$(python3 -c 'import json; print("/books/"+json.load(open("/tmp/reading-smoke.json"))[0]["id"])')
curl -sf "$base$loc" | python3 -c 'import sys; t=sys.stdin.read(); assert "The Left Hand of Darkness" in t; assert "Ursula K. Le Guin" in t; assert "Winter on Gethen." in t; assert "Link to this book" in t; print("detail ok")'
curl -sf -o /dev/null -D - -X POST "$base$loc/finish" --data 'next=/'
echo '--- home after finish ---'
curl -sf "$base/" | python3 -c 'import sys; t=sys.stdin.read(); i=t.index("Finished"); assert "The Left Hand of Darkness" in t[i:]; print("finished section ok")'"}
